correctness.rationale: The forbidden pair conditions are necessary by comparability and forced terminal-leaf selection. Sufficiency constructs Q from required positives and parents of negative leaves, proves Q incomparable and disjoint from negative queries, and covers remaining paths with unqueried leaves. Replacing each independent-set leaf by its parent proves the exact VC rank as the width of the internal tree. The comb has \(m+1\) explicit frontiers, all adjacent threshold cuts, an adaptive balanced-depth lower bound and a cardinality upper bound. The complete b-ary shattering recursion follows from cross-branch absence of conflicts. The standalone checker passed 6213 finite-tree cases plus regular-tree polynomial and comb online checks. One-vertex exception is excluded explicitly; no finite test substitutes for the proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The concepts can equivalently be described as complete tree frontiers, maximal prefix-free codes, or root–leaf cutsets. Those aliases were included in searches. A maximal-antichain counting polynomial is not the same as the polynomial of query supports shattered by their incidence vectors: a height-one rooted star already has the latter equal to \(1+(b+1)z\), while maximal antichains have sizes one and b. The comb equivalence is proved here, not inferred from a generic threshold title.

value.rationale: The all-tree pair-obstruction theorem proves that an entire natural family of shattering complexes is flag, determines every shattered support and exactly identifies its VC dimension. Its complete-b-ary specialization gives a constructive coefficientwise polynomial recursion and explicit leading coefficient, while the comb family establishes an unbounded logarithmic separation between static and adaptive learnability at fixed VC dimension one. These are structural facts about a motivated prefix-code/frontier concept class, not an isolated small enumeration or unmotivated parameter slice.
